disclosure_text: My parents are immigrants who moved to Canada when they were young. We lived in a muslim household.
micronarrative: I like that the community comes together to support the local bakery. I’ve seen similar events happen in my city, and sometimes the response is negative, but I appreciate diversity where I live. Canada is a melting pot of different religions and cultures, and I love that I can experience it all. I also appreciate finding authentic Lebanese food here because it reminds me of my home country. I don’t speak much Arabic, but I do try to when I’m ordering from them. It makes me feel a bit more connected to the owners. I understand how difficult it is to start over in a foreign country and adapt while still keeping your own customs alive. I think the boycotting hurts everyone involved. We need to support our community, including immigrants who are important in sustaining our mixed cultural roots.
